In Path 2, Acrivastine is connected to Dehydrogenase/reductase SDR family member 9, which is targeted by CID 6712947, and CID 6712947 is also linked to RWLeu4. Both pathways involve Acrivastine interacting with proteins that are targets of other entities, which in turn target RWLeu4. The integration of these pathways implies that Acrivastine may exert its effects through multiple molecular mechanisms that ultimately lead to the inhibition or modulation of RWLeu4. The evidence supports a mechanistic link between Acrivastine and RWLeu4, though the exact nature of the interaction remains to be fully elucidated. The presence of two distinct targets (Tubulin--tyrosine ligase and Dehydrogenase/reductase SDR family member 9) suggests that Acrivastine may act through different pathways, potentially modulating RWLeu4 through varied molecular mechanisms.
